text:
alex: Hey @people-ops — quick scenario: planning to take 8 weeks parental leave starting May 2, but want a phased return: 4 weeks at 60% FTE then full-time after. Questions: 1) How does a phased/part-time return interact with our review cycle in June? 2) Will bonus or equity vesting be pro-rated for the partial-months? 3) Do we need formal paperwork to change to 60% FTE temporarily? 4) Well need a short-term contractor backfill for oncall and a product launch sprint — what's the hiring ops flow? Also need clarity on health benefits premiums while hours are reduced.

michelle (People Ops): Congrats Alex! TL;DR: phased returns are supported. Details: managers complete reviews on schedule; reviewers should note "phased return" in calibration so expectations are fair. Bonus eligibility typically requires employment on the payout date; partial-month FTE won't automatically disqualify you but payouts can be prorated per plan rules. Equity vesting usually continues per plan docs. Please submit a Parental Leave Request and a Phased Return Request form so we have the official record.

riz (Benefits): For health benefits: if you're an active employee (even at 60% FTE) coverage usually continues but premium share may change. We need the effective date and will confirm if any premium remittance is required. If you drop below eligibility threshold, COBRA or company continuation options are discussed. I'll DM the exact eligibility thresholds and a sample premium calculation.

ana (ana (Manager)): From a manager perspective I'll approve the phased schedule if you commit to the 4-week ramp plan. For reviews: let's keep your review in June; I'll document the phased return in the calibration notes and focus on outcomes. For backfill: Sam from Hiring — can you advise?

sam (Hiring): We can spin up a 6-week contractor for the launch and oncall. Hiring ops checklist: 1) manager raises a short-term headcount req in Greenhouse tagged "contractor parental backfill", 2) procurement authorizes rate cap, 3) TA sources and we do a fast interview loop. Typical timeline is 10 business days if urgent. Ana, please open the req and mark the top skills and interview panel.

alex: Thanks — do I need to take any FMLA paperwork to get the phased return approved? I'm in CA.

michelle (People Ops): If you're in the US and eligible for FMLA, submit the FMLA certification if you want leave protection. Phased return arrangements can be part of an STD/RTW (short-term disability/return-to-work) accommodation if medically advised. Otherwise phased return is an agreed scheduling change — still document via the Phased Return Request form. We'll coordinate with Payroll for any pay adjustments.

payroll-bot: Reminder: any FTE change requires Payroll notification 30 days before effective date for accurate payroll scheduling. File the Phased Return Request at https://redwood.internal/hr/forms/phased-return.

riz (Benefits): Action items: Alex  send the effective dates and we'll send premium impact. Michelle  confirm whether FMLA certification is requested. Ana  open the contractor req in Greenhouse. Sam  TA to target 10 biz day turn.

it-bot: If Alex will keep company laptop while on phased return, open an Equipment Travel/Remote Access ticket for VPN and device insurance check.

alex: Submitted Parental Leave Request and Phased Return Request. Ana  Ill add the role spec for backfill by EOD. Thanks all :heart:
